account:
Today’s unusual business consists chiefly of unanswered questions, not confirmed wrongdoing. My scheduled mill inspection could not be completed: nobody presented grain stocks, and the operator and reserve-stock location remain unidentified. This does not establish a shortage. I approved the secretary’s draft asking the council to identify the operator and arrange a hosted inspection; delivery has not yet been confirmed.

There is also a vague rumour about a bridge or port change. At tea, the neighbour said they had spoken directly with the baker, who knew no verified proposal and asked that the rumour not be repeated as fact. The neighbour reported quiet docks and ordinary bread sales and orders. I have no evidence of a concrete transport project or its purpose.

The secretary’s records search found the four great-hall table chests empty, with no accounts ledger or commitments register. The accounts-review book is only meeting minutes. That is a records gap, not proof that there are no obligations or that funds have been misused. An earlier treasury balance of 128 emeralds was reported by me, but the secretary has not independently checked the balance or outstanding payments.

The innkeeper has asked generally about this week’s visitor demand, without supplying an occasion, dates, or numbers. I have asked the secretary to clarify those details without making commitments. It could be ordinary planning; I cannot yet link it to the transport rumour or the incomplete inspection. The secretary is helping gather records and arrange follow-up. I remain curious whether there is business happening without my knowledge, but presently have no verified explanation or evidence of a coordinated secret undertaking. My next scheduled engagement is home at nineteen hundred.
